newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Central bank appeal helps firm Taiwan money rates.
newsitem.headline: Central bank appeal helps firm Taiwan money rates.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed higher on Thursday, two days after central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said he hoped the overnight interbank would rise to five percent.
The interbank rate ended at 4.982 percent compared with Wednesday's 4.935 close, with the 30-day commercial paper at 5.00-5.10 against 4.75-4.85.

The central bank issued T$15 billion in NCDs to mop up liquidity in the past few days, but dealers said liquidity in the banking system remained loose and expected the interbank rate to hover around five percent in the near term.
In the government bond market, sentiment was cautious as the finance ministry was preparing to issue T$35 billion in seven-year bonds next week.
Dealers said they expected buying to turn conservative as the bond auction approaches.
